items.title: Private players should not replicate ISRO’s efforts: G Madhavan Nair writes
items.summary: India is at an important transition point in its space programme. The country is moving from a predominantly government-led space programme to an ecosystem in which private companies and startups can participate across the entire value chain. Indian Space Policy 2023 explicitly enables private entities to undertake activities including satellite realisation and operations, launch services, data acquisition and dissemination and ground infrastructure. ​The number of registered space startups has risen from one in 2014 to approximately 440 in 2026​, the government told the Rajya Sabha in August. The government also estimates India’s space economy at approximately US$9 billion in 2026, and predicts this will multiply to US$40–45 billion over the next decade. The question therefore is not whether India should encourage private participation in the space sector – the answer is obvious. items.title: Pre-ride tipping for cabs, autos under CCPA scanner: Why Rapido was fined but Namma Yatri wasn't
items.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has come down on pre-ride tipping mechanisms used by cab and auto ride aggregators, holding that a tip sought before a journey begins can effectively become a payment for preferential or faster service rather than a voluntary gratuity. In two separate orders concerning Rapido and Namma Yatri, the consumer regulator examined features that encouraged passengers to pay above the quoted fare in the hope of getting a ride faster. While the CCPA imposed a ₹10 lakh penalty on Rapido for misleading advertisements, unfair trade practices and dark patterns, it closed proceedings against Namma Yatri after noting that the latter had removed the offending prompt before the show cause notice and subsequently disabled its “extra fare” feature altogether. The two cases arose from the same complaint received by the CCPA on May 16, 2025 regarding manipulative pre-ride tipping and pricing practices across ride-hailing platforms. In Rapido’s case, the Authority took exception to prompts such as: “ Captains aren’t accepting at ₹60. Try adding +10, +20, +30 .” The platform also displayed the message: “Higher the price, higher the chance of getting a ride.

items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to urgently hear a petition filed by Wildlife SOS co-founder and CEO Kartick Satyanarayan challenging a Madhya Pradesh High Court order that withdrew his interim protection from arrest in an alleged leopard poaching case. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana agreed to list the plea this week after Senior Advocate Siddhartha Dave mentioned the matter for urgent hearing. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The case stems from a probe initiated by the Madhya Pradesh State Tiger Strike Force (STSF) concerning the alleged poaching of leopards, whose skins were recovered in Agra, Uttar Pradesh.
